paper.title_en: Compatibility of quantum trace and UV-IR maps
paper.abstract_en: This paper studies the connection between the quantum trace map [3,18,33] – which maps the <math altimg="si1.svg"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="fraktur">sl</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>-skein module to the quantum Teichmüller space for surfaces and to the quantum gluing module for 3-manifolds – and the quantum UV-IR map [31] – which maps the <math altimg="si2.svg"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="fraktur">gl</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>-skein module to the <math altimg="si3.svg"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="fraktur">gl</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>-skein module of the branched double cover. We show that the two maps are compatible in a precise sense, and that the compatibility map is natural under changes of triangulation; for surfaces, this resolves a conjecture of Neitzke and Yan [31]. As a corollary, under a mild hypothesis on the 3-manifold, the quantum trace map can be recovered from the quantum UV-IR map, hence providing yet another construction of the 3d quantum trace map recently introduced in [18,33].
